question.text: The following statements concern elements in the periodic table. Which of the following is true?

options.text: For group <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn></math> elements, the stability of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math> oxidation state increases down the group.

Elements of group <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>16</mn></math> have lower ionization enthalpy values compared to those of group <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn></math> in the corresponding periods.
The group <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>13</mn></math> elements are all metals.
All the elements in group <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>17</mn></math> are gases.

solution.text: Group 16 elements have less ionization potential than Group 15 elements due to half-filled configurations of group 15 elements. So need more amount of energy to remove an electron. In the halogen family iodine is solid and bromine is liquid. In the boron family boron is non metal.
